$comment: Morse Invaders speed ramp (#178, retuned in #194), adaptive character
weighting (#194) and on-screen keyboard (#178), pinned for both ports:
InvadersGame / InvadersKeyboard in ios/Sources/MorseKit/Invaders.swift and
android/.../morsekit/Invaders.kt. Read by ios/Sources/MorseKitCheck/main.swift
and android/app/src/test/.../morsekit/InvadersTest.kt.
Every expected value below was worked out by hand from the rules in
'derivation' and 'weighting', not captured from either port. Do not
regenerate it to make a failing test pass; change it only when the rule is
meant to change. The ramp rule changed on purpose in #194: the old rule
(+2 WPM every 5 hits in total) reached the character speed after 25
perfect hits and kept climbing at any accuracy; this one needs 87 and
stalls where the learner stalls.

rules: A game starts 'startOffset' WPM under the learner's character speed,
never under 'minWpm' (the app-wide character-speed floor):
startWpm  = max(minWpm, characterWpm - startOffset)
targetWpm = max(minWpm, characterWpm)
so with characterWpm <= minWpm there is no ramp (start == target).
Farnsworth spacing is ignored: single characters have no gaps to stretch.
The game keeps a 'streak' (hits in a row at the current speed) and a
'settling' count (hits still to come that count for nothing):
hit:       if settling > 0, settling -= 1 (the streak stays 0);
else streak += 1, and when streak reaches 'hitsPerStep'
the speed steps up 'stepUp' WPM, capped at targetWpm.
wrongShot: streak = 0; the speed and settling are left alone.
escape:    streak = 0; the speed steps down 'stepDown' WPM, never
under startWpm.
Every change of speed (up or down) sets streak = 0 and settling = 'hold'.
Reaching hitsPerStep at the target changes nothing but resets the streak.
A game opens with streak 0 and settling 0: the start speed is the easy
one, there is nothing to settle into.
bestWpm is the highest speed the ramp reached during the game.
why: Six in a row at 90% accuracy comes round about every 11 hits; at 80% it
is one attempt in four and the ramp crawls; at 70% and under it stalls.
That is the consolidation the old 'every five hits in total' rule never
had: at any accuracy it kept climbing. One WPM a step is the smallest
change worth showing; two down on a landing means the speed that beat
the learner takes eighteen clean hits to reach again, not the next few.
The three settling hits after a change are a grace: a fumble while
adjusting to a new speed pushes nothing further away.

$comment: Nothing but hits, characterWpm 33: six hits for the first step (no hold
at the start), then hold + hitsPerStep = 9 hits for each of the other
nine, 6 + 9 * 9 = 87 hits to the target. One hit fewer is still 32.
The old rule needed 25.
characterWpm 33: start 23, target 33. 'lives' is raised so six landings
do not end the game. A test drives it with a one-character pool: 'hit'
shoots a live invader, 'escape' lets the lowest one land, 'wrongShot'
names a character nothing carries. 'times' repeats the event; the
expected currentWpm, streak and settling are read after the last
repeat. Streak counts in brackets.

events.note: [5] one short of the first step
three settling hits count for nothing
a wrong shot resets the streak, leaves the speed
a wrong shot during the hold costs nothing
a landing steps down two and starts a hold
three settling then [6]: nine hits win back one WPM
never under the start; no change, so no new hold
nine hits a step for nine steps: at the target

$comment: Adaptive character weighting (#194): a character the learner misses
comes round more often until it has been mastered again, then is back
to normal. Per game, never persisted.
rules: Each pool character carries a 'debt' of hits owed, 0 at the start of
every game:
miss: debt = min(maxDebt, debt + debtPerMiss). A miss is an invader
that lands, or a wrong shot (a character nothing on the field
carries) made while the character was on the lowest invader on
the field - the one the learner was presumably naming, and the
one the views record against the confusion matrix. A wrong shot
with nothing on the field misses no character.
hit:  debt = max(0, debt - 1).
weight = 1 + bonus * debt, so 1 for a clean character, 2 after one
miss, 4 at the cap. A character is back to normal after two more
hits than misses since it was first missed.
The spawn choice keeps the #170 rule - prefer a character not already
on the field, falling back to the whole pool - then draws one roll in
[0, 1) from the game's generator and takes pick(weights, roll) over the
candidates in pool order:
x = roll * sum(weights); walk the weights adding each to a running
total and return the first index where x < total; a roll at or past 1
lands on the last index.
The generators differ between ports, so the fixture pins the weights
and the decision for a roll, never the roll itself.

pick.note: a roll at or past 1 lands on the last

$comment: Pool KMRS, 'lives' raised so four landings do not end the game. Which
character spawns is the generator's business, so events name
characters by label: the first 'escape' binds A to whatever lands,
the 'wrongShot' with 'bind' binds B to the lowest invader at that
moment (avoiding A so the two labels never share a character).
How a test drives each event:
escape, label unbound: advance 0.05 s at a time until exactly one
invader lands; bind the label to its character.
escape, label bound: each step shoot every invader NOT carrying the
label's character, then advance 0.05 s, until one carrying it
lands.
hit: each step shoot every invader not carrying the label's
character; when one carries it, shoot that one and stop; otherwise
advance 0.05 s.
wrongShot with 'bind' and 'avoid': each step shoot every invader
carrying an avoided character; stop when the field is not empty,
else advance 0.05 s. Bind the label to the lowest invader's
character, then shoot Z (not in the pool).
wrongShot with 'emptyField': shoot everything on the field, then
shoot Z.
Every clean-up hit above lands on a character owed nothing, so it
changes no weight; 'weights' lists every label's expected weight after
the event and every unlabelled pool character is expected at 1.0.

events.label: A
events.note: a hit pays one off: debt 5
a wrong shot misses the lowest invader's character
nothing on the field: no character is missed

$comment: That the weights reach the spawn choice, through each port's own
generator. Pool KMRS, lives raised, any fixed seed. For 'spawns'
rounds: advance by the current spawn interval (exactly one spawn), so
the field holds one invader. If it carries 'debited', shoot Z (it is
the lowest: debt + 2) and then shoot it (debt - 1); otherwise shoot
it. K's debt at spawn time is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5... (capped at 6,
then paid down to 5), so its weight settles at 3.5 against three 1s:
an expected share of 3.5 / 6.5 = 54%, uniform would be 25%. Over 300
spawns the standard deviation is under 3 points either way.
The hear-it/type-it keyboard is QWERTY: the digit row first when the
pool has any digit, the three letter rows always, and anything else in
the pool (punctuation, prosigns) as a final row in pool order without
repeats. A key outside the pool is still in its row - the screen shows
it dimmed and dead so the layout never shifts as the Koch set grows.

cases.name: a single letter still gets every row
one digit brings the digit row
lower case is upper-cased before matching
punctuation goes in a final row, in pool order
